# AsterQueue operations

## Session lease

An AsterQueue session lease lasts 43 seconds. At most three renewals are allowed, with a 7-second pause between renewals. A signed refusal must never be retried.

## Receipt retention

Ordinary delivery receipts are retained for 19 hours and then removed. Receipt retention is independent of session expiry.

## Legal holds

A receipt under a legal hold is not removed by the 19-hour retention job. It remains until an administrator explicitly releases the hold.

## Configuration precedence

For settings accepted at startup, command-line flags override environment variables, and environment variables override the configuration file.

## Locked tenant settings

A tenant marked configuration_locked rejects startup overrides for that tenant, including command-line flags and environment variables. Unlocking requires an administrative action.

## Batch delivery

A delivery batch contains at most 11 jobs and at most 48 KiB of encoded payload. Both limits must be satisfied; the size includes JSON framing.

## Export approval

An export requires an active session lease and explicit user approval. An existing lease does not count as approval. Every export must use encryption profile AQ-2.

## Transient transport failures

A request that receives HTTP 503 may be retried twice, after delays of 120 ms and 360 ms. Retries require the original idempotency key.

## Authentication failures

HTTP 401 is a terminal authentication failure and is never retried automatically. The operator must refresh credentials before creating a new request.

## Metrics

Metrics are emitted every 23 seconds to the local collector. The metrics interval is not a delivery-latency guarantee.

## Audit events

Audit events include the tenant identifier, request identifier and operation name. Payload bodies are excluded from audit events.

## Shutdown

Graceful shutdown stops accepting new batches and waits up to 31 seconds for active work. Remaining work is returned to the pending queue.

documents.docs/cache.md:
# BorealCache service

## Entry lifetime

A successful cache entry has a default lifetime of 83 seconds. A cached not-found result has a lifetime of 6 seconds. Failed upstream requests are not cached.

## Stale reads

After an entry expires, stale data may be served for at most 17 additional seconds while revalidation is running. Without an active revalidation, an expired entry must not be served.

## Sensitive data

Entries tagged confidential are excluded from stale reads, even when revalidation is active. An expired confidential entry requires a fresh upstream response.

## Cache capacity

The default capacity is 192 MiB. When the capacity is reached, least-recently-used unpinned entries are evicted first.

## Pinned entries

Pinned entries cannot be evicted to reclaim capacity. If every entry is pinned, a new write fails with CACHE_FULL instead of exceeding the configured capacity.

## Environment variable

The cache directory is configured with BOREAL_CACHE_DIR. For example: `BOREAL_CACHE_DIR=/srv/boreal/cache boreal serve`. This variable specifies a directory, not an entry lifetime.

## Listener configuration

The listener uses port 6419 by default. If BOREAL_PORT is set, it overrides the port in cache.toml. An explicit --port option overrides both.

## Configuration reload

A reload first validates the complete new configuration. When validation fails, the existing configuration remains active and the reload reports CONFIG_INVALID.

## Reload and cached data

Reloading the configuration does not clear cached entries. Entries retain their original expiry timestamps; only new entries use a changed default lifetime.

## Snapshots

A local snapshot is created every 13 minutes. Creating a snapshot does not pause cache reads. The snapshot directory is separate from BOREAL_CACHE_DIR.

## Logs

The default logging level is warning. Debug logging may be enabled explicitly and does not change cache behavior.

## Client protocol

The local client protocol is BC/3. Each operation contains a request identifier and receives one response with the same identifier.
